thread.title: Apple iPhone Partner Foxconn Is Bracing for a 'Very Difficult' Year

author: Barron's
title: Apple iPhone Partner Foxconn Is Bracing for a 'Very Difficult' Year
text:
Photograph by Qilai Shen/Bloomberg Apple's largest iPhone assembly partner Foxconn plans to reduce expenses by $2.9 billion in 2019 as it faces "a very difficult and competitive year," according to a new report.
Bloomberg, citing an internal Foxconn memo, reports that the company also plans to cut 10% of its non-technical staff. Foxconn's cost-cutting announcement is the latest of round news pointing to weaker than expected demand for Apple's newly released iPhones .
Apple stock ( AAPL ) was up 0.6% to $178.07 on Wednesday morning.
"The review being carried out by our team this year is no different than similar exercises carried out in past years to ensure that we enter into each new year with teams and budgets that are aligned with the current and anticipated needs of our customers, our global operations and the market and economic challenges of the next year or two," a Foxconn spokesperson said in an emailed statement to Barron's.
Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Apple stock has fallen more than 18% this month as investors grow increasingly worried about iPhone sales given warnings from suppliers and negative commentary by analysts.
Read more : Apple Stock Could Keep Falling. Here's Why
On Monday, The Wall Street Journal , citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models.
Last week, wireless chip maker Qorvo ( QRVO ) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12.
Earlier this month, the Nikkei Asian Review also reported that Apple told its suppliers to cancel plans for additional iPhone XR production lines.
